newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Foreign investment in Colombia reaches record high.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Colombia reaches record high.

text.p: A record-high $472 million in direct foreign investment, excluding stocks and the volatile oil sector, entered Colombia in November 1996, the country's foreign investment board said.
It said the figure, inflated by a Spanish bank's purchase of a 40 percent stake in Banco Ganadero, marked a 657 percent increase over November 1996.
It also marked the highest monthly inflow of direct foreign investment in Colombian history, according to the investment board, known as Coinvertir.

Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya accounted for $327 million of total direct foreign investment in November. The payment was made for 40 percent of the voting stock of Ganadero, Colombia's largest commercial bank.

Foreign investment in Colombia's stock market rose to $24 million in November. The figure marks a huge increase, said by Coinvertir to total 1,310 percent, over the same period in 1995. Colombia's stock markets posted million dollar losses in November 1995 because of the political crisis and widespread uncertainty stemming from allegations against President Ernesto Samper.
